evidence_detail: AUTHORITATIVE eps=36.1. Traced byte-identical through dielectric_v04.csv (row 227, dielectric=36.1, source_doi=10.1016/j.isci.2026.115778, source_table='Table 3') -> condition_pair_validity_v1.csv (v04row-227.v04_dielectric=36.1) -> gap_aggregation_audit.csv (gap_epsilon=36.1) -> admission_review_queue (dielectric_raw=36.1). Four of five tables agree. THE ONE DISSENTER IS gap_aggregation_audit.csv v04_epsilon=36.9, which is WRONG and is the exact cell the pre-fix queue code read. ROOT CAUSE (code defect): scripts/confirm_2027/audit_gap_aggregation_provenance.py:523 builds v04_by_skeleton = {skeleton(inchikey): row} where skeleton()=inchikey.split('-')[0] (line 161-163). That dict keeps only the LAST row per skeleton, so both v04row-227 and v04row-248 resolve to the SAME v04 row (the 36.9 one). v04_epsilon is therefore 36.9 for BOTH audit rows. Confirmed: 3 of 248 rows are corrupted this way (R166 2.062->2, R174 9.2->2.14, R227 36.1->36.9); all 3 are in the 3 duplicated-skeleton groups (ZQDPJFUHLCOCRG cis/trans-3-hexene, KFUSEUYYWQURPO cis/trans-1,2-dichloroethene, GAEKPEKOJKCEMS). gap_epsilon is CORRECT on all 248 rows and is the authoritative column. WHY HOLD: not a value error but an evidentiary one. measurement_ledger_v1.csv has 0 rows for this InChIKey (verified, 2065 rows / 153 InChIKeys, all sourced from data/processed/dielectric_observations_v11plus.csv = ThermoML only; GVL has 0 rows there). So NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENTS is correct and condition_pair_valid=false is correct, with the right reason. Ingestion path is manual/NBS-style, NOT ThermoML: the 36.1 leg came from data/processed/modern_solvent_public_review_observations.csv (open-access review table, dataset_origin=v0.3_addition), carrying no source_file/source_row_index, which is why it never enters the ledger. T_K=298.15 is NOT a measurement: temperature_source='review_table_standard_room_temperature' (imputed); all 21 such rows in v04 are pinned to exactly 298.15. The 298.15 K agreement between the two rows is therefore an artefact of two different imputations, not independent corroboration. SECONDARY DEFECT (annotation): dielectric_v04_provenance_patches.csv and the v04 notes call 36.1 'the beta lactone value', but the row's own SMILES CC1CCC(=O)O1 / InChIKey GAEKPEKOJKCEMS-UHFFFAOYSA-N is a FIVE-membered gamma-lactone, not a beta-lactone. The label contradicts the row's own structure.

AUTHORITATIVE eps=36.9. Consistent in ALL tables: dielectric_v04.csv row 248 dielectric=36.9 (source_doi=10.1016/j.ica.2021.120372, source_quality=primary, source_table='supporting information') -> pv v04row-248.v04_dielectric=36.9 -> gap_epsilon=36.9 -> gap.v04_epsilon=36.9 -> queue dielectric_raw=36.9. NO value discrepancy on this row. It escaped the skeleton-join corruption ONLY BY POSITION: it is the last row of the GAEKPEKOJKCEMS group, and dict-comprehension overwrite leaves the last row intact. Had row order been reversed, R248 would have read 36.1 and R227 36.9 -- the corruption is positional, not substantive. code_defect_found=true on that basis. WHY HOLD: identical structural defect to R227. Zero ledger rows for this InChIKey; verdict_reason=NO_BAND_OBSERVATIONS_FOUND; n_contributing_measurements=0; condition_pair_valid=false with invalidity_reason=NO_CONTRIBUTING_MEASUREMENTS (correct, and not masking anything else). T_K=298.15 is IMPUTED, not measured: temperature_source='not_reported' -- it is the single such row in v04. The 36.9 value traces upstream to data/raw/reaxys_w17c/observations.csv (Reaxys substance card, CAS 108-29-2, value=36.9, T_K EMPTY) and was then attached to the Segato 2021 DOI by manual Crossref resolution; the Reaxys queue row also mislabelled the InChIKey as JYVATQXCHBTGRN-UHFFFAOYSA-N (correctly corrected to GAEKPEKOJKCEMS-UHFFFAOYSA-N). So the 298.15 K pairing is an imputation on one side and an imputation on the other. Per the project's own source-quality rule the primary SI leg is the stronger leg, so compound-level the authoritative eps is 36.9; per-row the authoritative value is each row's own master value, nothing averaged.
